subject: Media Literacy
title: Newsroom Demographics and Blind Spots
description: One-minute skill: Newsroom Demographics and Blind Spots.

hook.text: Most newsroom leaders are white, college-educated, and live in major cities. They cover a country that isn't.

buildup.text: Newsroom demographics shape coverage. Stories from unfamiliar communities get less nuanced treatment.

discovery.text: A newsroom that doesn't reflect its audience produces blind spots — entire communities and issues go unseen.

twist.text: Diversity in newsrooms isn't just a fairness issue. It directly affects what stories get covered and how.

climax.text: When the people telling the stories don't represent the people in them, the stories are inevitably incomplete.

punchline.text: Who's in the newsroom decides which stories get told.

quiz.question: How do newsroom demographics affect coverage?
options: They don't — all journalists are objective
Homogeneous newsrooms create blind spots where entire communities go unseen
More diverse newsrooms produce worse content
